items.title: Renault Duster 1.3 Turbo To Become Rs 1.5 Lakh Cheaper: Here's Why

items.title: Tamil Nadu government restructures crop loan waiver scheme, extends eligibility period by a month
points: Rao The Tamil Nadu government has restructured the crop loan waiver scheme, announcing a waiver of ₹75,000 for farmers who obtained loans exceeding ₹75,000 from cooperative institutions.
Farmers who obtained crop loans of up to ₹75,000 will continue to receive a full waiver of the loan amount.

Earlier, the arrangement was that farmers who had obtained loans ranging from ₹75,000 to ₹1 lakh would receive a maximum waiver of ₹75,000, while those who had borrowed more than ₹1 lakh would be given a maximum waiver of ₹35,000.
The government has also extended the eligibility period by a month, covering loans obtained by farmers up to March 31, 2026.
The State government has sanctioned an additional ₹2,842.77 crore towards the implementation of the expanded scheme.
The total expenditure on the revised crop loan waiver scheme is estimated at ₹9,062.83 crore, of which ₹6,220.056 crore has already been released.

items.title: IAF's IL-76MD completes landing in highest-altitude ever touchdown by the plane
points: The Indian Air Force on Saturday scripted history as an IL-76 MD transport aircraft of Russian origin successfully landed at the Nyoma air base in Ladakh, achieving the highest-altitude touchdown achieved by the plane anywhere in the world.
The Nyoma airbase is located at a height of around 13,000 ft and is at a distance of around 25 km from the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China.
The Ilyushin IL-76 MD, called 'Gajraj' by the IAF, is a multipurpose four-engine turbofan strategic airlifter that is designed to carry heavy cargo weighing about 40 tonnes.
Landing at a high-altitude base like Nyoma was a challenging task, as the thin air reduces engine thrust and lift.

On November 12, 2025, then-Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh inaugurated the Mudh-Nyoma airbase in Ladakh, designed as the world's highest fighter-capable airfield, by landing a C-130J special operations aircraft there.
The air base was located at 13,700 feet and was constructed at an estimated cost of ₹218 crore.

items.title: Rates Blow-Up Triggers Rush for Cash at Austrian Property Funds
points: (Bloomberg) -- The surge in global interest rates may be a tipping point for a handful of Austrian open-ended real estate funds that for years have defied one of Europe’s most troubled property markets.
Austria is home to one of Europe’s largest ongoing insolvencies: the 2023 meltdown of Rene Benko’s €23 billion ($25.7 billion) property empire.
Non-performing loan ratios for some types of Austrian commercial real estate have topped 14%.
To be sure, the funds have invested prudently and returned an average of 2% to 2.4% annually over the past 10 years.

That was an attractive performance for an asset assumed to offer daily liquidity in the years of negative borrowing costs, but has lost its appeal with the European Central Bank’s main rate at 2.5% and likely to rise again as soon as next month.
Bank Austria’s Real Invest fund manages about €2.4 billion worth of properties, mostly in the largest Austrian cities.
Erste’s Immobilienfonds holds €1.3 billion, including about 45% in German assets.
